blockers.title: The new-generation sequence rule simultaneously requires restart and cross-generation numeric nonreuse.
blockers.finding: grantGenerationClosure says a new grant generation is a new carrier with sequence restarting at its own origin and MUST NOT reuse the closed generation's sequence numbers; backupRestore repeats continuation only in a new generation without sequence reuse. Those requirements cannot both govern the unsigned integer ordinal as written. A restart at the new carrier's origin repeats ordinary low numeric values used by the closed carrier. Avoiding every prior numeric value instead requires a global cross-generation allocator or high-water state. But permission-truth-tables.v6 makes the journal and its strictly increasing sequence per (project, grant generation), derives next solely from that journal, and explicitly says comparing different generations is undefined and unneeded. v7 therefore either contradicts the accepted DR-105 namespace or silently invents cross-generation durable state without class, owner, writer, backup, or recovery rules.
blockers.requiredRepair: Choose one namespace explicitly. The compatible repair is to define the unique order key as (project, grant generation, sequence), allow the numeric sequence to restart per new carrier, and state that nonreuse applies only within a carrier; update backupRestore to say the closed generation's tuple is never reused. If global numeric nonreuse is actually required, route that change through DR-105 and assign the global allocator/high-water bytes a complete DR-124 class and lifecycle. Do not leave both rules operative.

blockers.title: The terminal-marker MUST conflicts with three states that categorically forbid further appends.
blockers.finding: projectPurge unconditionally MUST append exactly one grant-journal-terminal-marker. Yet backupRestore makes a witnessless restored generation permanently fail-closed to further appends; grantGenerationClosure appends its marker and then refuses further appends; and FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN permits no new appends. Project purge after any of those reachable states requires an append the same contract forbids. The generation-closure/project-purge order also leaves two clauses each phrased as an append action without defining the second as an idempotent observation of the already-existing marker. This is not an implementation detail: no state machine can satisfy all of the unconditional MUSTs, and witnessless restore cannot safely append a marker because the missing tail makes the next ordinal unknowable.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define one carrier terminalization state machine with precedence and idempotence. For a healthy open carrier, the first qualifying closure may append exactly one marker and atomically make the carrier terminal; later purge/closure events must observe that marker and perform no append. For a witnessless restore or FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN carrier, define a non-appending purge/closure branch and the durable, classed fact that keeps it fail-closed, or declare the restore unsuccessful and keep the carrier quarantined. Make clear how crash recovery distinguishes OPEN, TERMINAL, WITNESSLESS-FROZEN, and OVERTURN-FROZEN without reusing sequence or minting purge/D9 authority.
